analysis.investment_thesis: Crompton is a sound consumer electricals franchise with minimal debt (D/E 0.05) and a 7-year positive earnings record, but the price of INR 261 offers no margin of safety — it trades at 2.6× my Graham Number of ~INR 100 (sqrt(22.5 × EPS ~8.6 × BVPS ~51.9)). At P/E 34.4 and P/B 4.93, the market is paying a growth premium that the cautious investor has no business paying.
key_strengths: Near-zero leverage: D/E of 0.05 and borrowings collapsed from INR 1,686 Cr (2022) to INR 186 Cr (2025), demonstrating disciplined post-acquisition debt repayment
Consistent operating cash generation: OCF positive all 5 years reviewed (INR 411–843 Cr range), FCF positive every year including INR 635 Cr in 2025
Long earnings track record: 7 consecutive years of positive net profit (INR 324–617 Cr), satisfying my minimum history requirement
key_risks: Earnings have declined from the 2021 peak of INR 617 Cr to INR 442 Cr in 2024, only partially recovering to INR 564 Cr in 2025 — the Butterfly Gandhimathi acquisition disrupted margin stability
Operating margin of only 7.99% leaves little buffer; any input cost spike or competitive pricing pressure can rapidly erode thin profits
P/E of 34.4 embeds optimistic growth assumptions; if net profit growth continues at its 7Y CAGR of 8.2%, the growth story cannot justify this premium
red_flags: P/B of 4.93 — paying nearly 5× book value for a consumer durables manufacturer with no unique proprietary assets
Net profit declined three consecutive years (FY22–FY24) while revenue grew — a margin compression alarm
Graham Number ~INR 100 versus market price INR 261: the stock requires earnings and book value to roughly double before it reaches fair value by my standards
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Crompton's financial profile is that of a respectable but fully-priced consumer brand. Revenue has compounded at 9.8% over seven years (INR 4,080 Cr to INR 7,864 Cr) and the balance sheet has been substantially repaired after the debt-funded Butterfly acquisition in FY22 inflated borrowings to INR 1,686 Cr — now down to INR 186 Cr. Operating cash flows are reliable and free cash flow averaged INR 652 Cr over the last three years. These are the characteristics of a well-run business.

However, my discipline begins and ends with price. At INR 261, the stock trades at P/E 34.4 and P/B 4.93 — more than double my maximum acceptable thresholds of 15 and 1.5 respectively. The Graham Number (sqrt(22.5 × ~8.6 EPS × ~51.9 BVPS)) yields roughly INR 100, meaning the current price embeds 2.6× the margin Mr. Market should be asking for. An intelligent investor waits for Mr. Market's pessimism to offer the stock nearer that figure.
